answer.rationale: The contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so switching primary vendor (memory_c2's past savings notwithstanding) or deferring decision both introduce unacceptable delivery risk this cycle. Adding a second source is valuable but cannot be stood up in 14 days and doesn't address the 18% cost mandate immediately. Negotiating terms with the incumbent — benchmarking-driven renegotiation (memory_c4) plus a multi-year/volume commitment for unit-cost reduction (memory_c6) — is the only lever that cuts cost without migration or interruption, consistent with memory_c1's stability record. Verifying c4 and c6 to confirm the magnitude and conditions of those savings before committing to a longer term.
